cards.text: Proverbs opens as the proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel (Proverbs 1:1). Here the writer talks to someone he calls my son, and he opens with a big if: if you've put up security for your neighbor, if you've shaken hands on a pledge with a stranger. Friend, that's the 'what could possibly go wrong' handshake.

cards.question: The writer keeps going with the ifs. If a pledge like that has trapped the son, what did the trapping?

answers.text: The words of his own mouth
A thief hiding by the road
A debt his father left him

cards.text: The writer says the son has fallen into his neighbor's hands. Friend, it's like texting 'sure, I'll help you move,' and now your Saturday, your back AND your truck belong to somebody else.

cards.question: To get free, the writer tells the son to go to his neighbor, ___ himself, and press his plea.
True or false: The writer tells the son that going to his neighbor to get free can wait until after a good night's sleep.

cards.text: No sleep for the eyes, no slumber for the eyelids, and the writer says to get free like a gazelle from the hand of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler. Friend, this is not a snooze-button problem, this is a one-sock-on, keys-in-your-teeth, out-the-door problem.
Then the writer calls out the slacker, and he hands the slacker a teacher straight from the animal world.

cards.question: Which creature does the writer tell the slacker to learn from?

cards.text: The writer says to observe its ways and become wise. A grown person, sent to take notes from a BUG, and friend, I'd be sitting right there in the front row with a pencil in my mustache.

cards.question: True or false: The ant gets its work done with no commander, overseer or ruler over it.
With no commander standing over it, when does the ant prepare its provisions?

cards.text: Then the writer asks the slacker how long he'll lie there and when he'll get up from his sleep. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer and couldn't get up if I tried, and this slacker can just... GET UP.

cards.question: True or false: The writer warns the slacker about one long, heavy sleep.
After a little sleep, a little slumber and a little folding of the hands, the writer warns the slacker that ___ will come upon him like a robber.

cards.text: Poverty like a robber, need like a bandit. Friend, that's two guests nobody invited, and neither one came for the cookies.
New picture now. The writer describes a worthless person, a wicked man who walks around with a perverse mouth.

cards.question: This wicked man doesn't only talk with his mouth. What else does he talk with?

answers.text: His eyes and feet and fingers
Songs and riddles at the gate

cards.text: Winking his eyes, speaking with his feet, pointing with his fingers. This man is a whole group chat, and he's typing with his ENTIRE body.

cards.question: The writer says this winking, pointing wicked man devises evil with ___ in his heart.
On top of devising evil, what does this wicked man continually sow?

cards.text: Then the writer says therefore, and friend, everything this man has been planting is going to come up.

cards.question: What does the writer say will come upon the wicked man?

answers.text: A slow and quiet decline over time

cards.text: In an instant, shattered beyond recovery, like a cookie hitting a tile floor. There is no five-second rule for THAT, friend.
Then the writer gives a list: six things the LORD hates, seven that are detestable to Him. Lean in, friend, because number one is haughty eyes.

cards.question: True or false: A lying tongue is on the list of things the LORD hates.
The LORD's list goes on to hands that shed innocent blood. Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands. What do the first three things on the list have in common?

answers.text: Each one is a part of the body
Each one is a sin of the priests
Each one is a sin against parents

cards.question: Next on the LORD's list is a heart that devises wicked schemes, and then come feet. What do those feet do?

cards.text: Number six on the list: a false witness who gives false testimony. One more to go.

Number seven, the last one: one who stirs up discord among brothers, the same discord the wicked man kept sowing. So the one whose hobby is starting drama? This is NOT the shout-out they were hoping for.
